bindings.objects: Landlord (Respondent); Family members (Wife, Son, Son's wife, Children)
bindings.event: Tribunal finding on family size vs. premises extent
Tribunal finding on suitability of alternative accommodation

evidence.record: The respondent was the owner of the entire premises and was occupying the ground floor at the time of the application.
The landlord required the premises bona fide for his occupation as a residence himself and his family members.
The tenant contended that the landlord's requirement for his occupation was not bona fide.
The Rent Controller accepted the tenant's plea that the requirement of the landlord for his occupation was not bona fide.
The High Court accepted the joint representation that the Tribunal had not recorded a finding on reasonably suitable residential accommodation and remanded the case.
The Tribunal held that the portion of premises in the landlord's occupation was not reasonably sufficient for a family consisting of the landlord, his wife, his son, son's wife and their children.
The Tribunal recorded a finding that the premises in the occupation of the respondent were not reasonably suitable for his residence.

limitations.reason: The claim of bona fide requirement is a party assertion contradicted by the Tribunal's prior finding; the target court has not yet accepted the bona fide element.
The High Court explicitly remanded the case for a finding on reasonably suitable accommodation, meaning no prior finding on this specific element exists for the target court to accept.

The Tribunal finding addresses the family size vs. premises sufficiency but does not explicitly map to the 'dependent family member' branch of the occupation route without further analysis of dependency status.

The Tribunal finding states the premises were not 'reasonably sufficient' for the family, but the statutory test requires 'reasonably suitable residential accommodation' for the landlord or such person; the precise legal equivalence is not established by the supplied text.

coverage_limits: The supplied law does not define 'bona fide', 'dependent', or 'reasonably suitable residential accommodation', preventing definitive assessment of ADDR-002, ADDR-005, and ADDR-008.
The High Court remanded the case, so no target-stage acceptance exists for any element of the clause (e) ground.
The identity between the 'landlord' and 'such person' for whom premises are held is not resolved, leaving the alternative occupation route (ADDR-007/ADDR-008) partially untested.
